Topics · Is the Quran from God?

What would a real message from God look like?

Write your test first. Then the Quran's four: consistency, challenge, his record, his gain. Each has a limit.

Part 1 of 4

﴿أَفَلَا يَتَدَبَّرُونَ ٱلْقُرْءَانَ ۚ وَلَوْ كَانَ مِنْ عِندِ غَيْرِ ٱللَّهِ لَوَجَدُوا۟ فِيهِ ٱخْتِلَـٰفًا كَثِيرًا﴾

Translation of the meaning

Then do they not reflect upon the Qur’ān?[203] If it had been from [any] other than Allāh, they would have found within it much contradiction.

Translator's notes

[203] i.e., its meanings and its objective.

Quran · An-Nisa 4:82

Translation

“Every word of God is flawless. He is a shield to those who take refuge in him. Don’t you add to his words, lest he reprove you, and you be found a liar.

Original · Hebrew

כָּל־אִמְרַ֣ת אֱל֣וֹהַּ צְרוּפָ֑ה מָגֵ֥ן ה֝֗וּא לַֽחֹסִ֥ים בּֽוֹ׃ אַל־תּ֥וֹסְףְּ עַל־דְּבָרָ֑יו פֶּן־יוֹכִ֖יחַ בְּךָ֣ וְנִכְזָֽבְתָּ׃

Proverbs · 30:5-6

World English Bible

Write your test first. Most people's lists share a few things: the message should not contradict itself; it should not be useful to whoever delivers it; it should tell you something its source could not easily have known; it should make you better, not only more certain. The verse sets a test of its own, and it is on that list: look for contradictions. It invites the search instead of forbidding it.

A question for you

Write your test in one line: what would a message have to be like for you to take it seriously?

Part 2 of 4

﴿وَإِن كُنتُمْ فِى رَيْبٍ مِّمَّا نَزَّلْنَا عَلَىٰ عَبْدِنَا فَأْتُوا۟ بِسُورَةٍ مِّن مِّثْلِهِۦ وَٱدْعُوا۟ شُهَدَآءَكُم مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ إِن كُنتُمْ صَـٰدِقِينَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And if you are in doubt about what We have sent down [i.e., the Qur’ān] upon Our Servant [i.e., Prophet Muḥammad (ﷺ)], then produce a sūrah the like thereof and call upon your witnesses [i.e., supporters] other than Allāh, if you should be truthful.

Quran · Al-Baqarah 2:23

The second test is a challenge. If you doubt it, bring something like it. It does not ask you to believe; it asks you to try to match. The honest limit: much of the test lies in the Arabic, so it works best for those who read the language. Anyone else cannot run it fully, and may say so. That nobody ever matched it cannot be measured in a way that settles the matter. It is a claim the book makes and its readers weigh, not a laboratory result.

A question for you

Could you run this test?

If you sayI read Arabic; I could
ThenThen it is open to you directly. Read it aloud, and try writing a line in its register yourself. Both are fair ways to test.
If you sayI cannot; I would have to trust others
ThenThen it is honest to say this test is not yet yours. The other tests here do not depend on Arabic, and you can treat this one as not yet run.
If you sayTaste in language is too subjective to count
ThenThat is a serious objection. Taste varies, and great poetry in any language is admired without being called divine. For that reason this test is hard to use alone, and it is best read together with the others.

Part 3 of 4

﴿قُل لَّوْ شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ مَا تَلَوْتُهُۥ عَلَيْكُمْ وَلَآ أَدْرَىٰكُم بِهِۦ ۖ فَقَدْ لَبِثْتُ فِيكُمْ عُمُرًا مِّن قَبْلِهِۦٓ ۚ أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Say, "If Allāh had willed, I would not have recited it to you, nor would He have made it known to you, for I had remained among you a lifetime before it.[516] Then will you not reason?"

Translator's notes

[516] The Prophet (ﷺ) lived among his people forty years before receiving any revelation.

Quran · Yunus 10:16

A third test is about the messenger. What do you know of the person bringing it? The verse offers his own history as evidence: he lived among his people for decades before saying anything of the kind, and they knew him. A test of character can be checked, at least by those who knew him: what was he like when there was nothing to gain? That is a question for history, and a fair one. The verse asks only whether you will use your reason on it.

A question for you

What would you want to know about a person before taking their message seriously?

If you sayTheir record before they spoke
ThenThen the verse meets you on your own ground. It is a question of history rather than belief, and you can look.
If you sayWhat they gain or lose by it
ThenThe next part is about exactly that.
If you sayWhether they live by it
ThenA fair test, and another that can be checked against the record.
If you sayWhether they say the hard parts too
ThenA good one. The book records rebukes addressed to the Prophet himself, and a later question here takes that up.

Part 4 of 4

﴿أُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ هَدَى ٱللَّهُ ۖ فَبِهُدَىٰهُمُ ٱقْتَدِهْ ۗ قُل لَّآ أَسْـَٔلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ أَجْرًا ۖ إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا ذِكْرَىٰ لِلْعَـٰلَمِينَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Those are the ones whom Allāh has guided, so from their guidance take an example. Say, "I ask of you for it [i.e., this message] no payment. It is not but a reminder for the worlds."

Quran · Al-An'am 6:90

A fourth test is gain. The verse has him say: I ask you for no payment for this; it is only a reminder for everyone. A messenger who profits from the message gives you reason to wonder. One who loses, who is mocked and refused, gives you a different data point. This is not proof either, since sincere people are often mistaken. It is a filter against fraud, not a proof of truth, and it moves the odds.

A question for you

How much weight does it deserve?

If you sayA lot
ThenIt does carry weight as a filter. Keep in mind that it screens out fraud, not error.
If you sayA little
ThenThat is probably about right: informative, but it settles little by itself.
If you sayNone; sincerity does not make it true
ThenA fair line to draw. Sincere people are often wrong, so this test can say only that the messenger is not obviously a fraud, never that the message is true.

The same in the other books

Translation

If anyone desires to do his will, he will know about the teaching, whether it is from God or if I am speaking from myself. He who speaks from himself seeks his own glory, but he who seeks the glory of him who sent him is true, and no unrighteousness is in him.

Original · Ancient Greek

ἐάν τις θέλῃ τὸ θέλημα αὐτοῦ ποιεῖν, γνώσεται περὶ τῆς διδαχῆς πότερον ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ ἐστιν ἢ ἐγὼ ἀπʼ ἐμαυτοῦ λαλῶ. ὁ ἀφʼ ἑαυτοῦ λαλῶν τὴν δόξαν τὴν ἰδίαν ζητεῖ· ὁ δὲ ζητῶν τὴν δόξαν τοῦ πέμψαντος αὐτὸν οὗτος ἀληθής ἐστιν καὶ ἀδικία ἐν αὐτῷ οὐκ ἔστιν.

the Gospel (John) · 7:17-18

World English Bible

Your reflection

If a message were true, what would you hope it would ask of you? Write that down, and then check whether the book you are reading asks it.
